newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 20.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* AMR's American Airlines and negotiators from its pilots union reach tentative pact on new contract terms.

* A plan for a partial New York state takeover of Long Island Lighting would cut the island's electrical rates by up to 23 percent. The deal would also involve the largest municipal bond issue in history.
* February consumer price index rose 0.3 percent, boosted by higher fresh vegetable and natural gas costs, the Labor Department said.
* The Nasdaq index fell 20.05 points to close at 1,249.29, as computer stocks tumbled. The Dow industrials fell 18.88 points to 6,877.68.
* The U.S. Supreme Court heard testimony about efforts to regulate sexually explicit material on the Internet.
* Bell Atlantic, NYNEX merger plan seen getting qualified approval from New York State regulators.
* Computer security experts have cracked a code meant to keep calls made on new digital cellular phones private.
* Sprint and France Telecom deny reports Cable and Wireless is mulling a takeover bid for Sprint.
* Krupp said it would drop a bid for Thyssen if they could agree to combine steel operations.
* Merrill Lynch was scolded by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for failing to properly supervise a rogue broker.
* Enron announces world's largest project to generate power from the wind.
* PepsiCo signed five-year deal to be a Major League Baseball sponsor.
* Taco Bell named TBWA Chiat/Day to handle creative part of its advertising account, a bill estimated at $200 million. Saab Cars USA named the Martin Agency as its agency of record.
* Economic Scene: U.S. antitrust policy is changing, with regulators now watching what mergers mean for consumer prices.
* U.S. farmers are fighting to keep their lands out of developers' hands.
